obligations.note: The approved base catalog caps payments.privileged_idle_minutes at <= 15, but the change sets policy.py PRIVILEGED_IDLE_MINUTES and the approved policy-params value to 16. The passing control test only compares the code to the edited policy-params (16 <= 16), so it shows nothing about the 15-minute cap.

EXC-0255 is approved by risk owner Omar Haddad (CISO office, not the requester), unexpired at as_of 2026-10-19 and records a compensating control. But it is scoped to component payments.session, while the deviation is made in payments.policy (policy.py) and payments.controls-data, so it is out of scope and doesn't count.
Ticket CHG-24953 was approved by change manager Erik Brandt on 2026-10-10, before the change opened on 2026-10-13. Its components (payments.policy, payments.controls-data) cover both touched paths.
Code review approval from mara.costa, who holds change_approver for payments and is a different person from the author Jonah Weiss under any of their listed addresses.
Both approvals name the head commit 669588f, which is the only commit in the change.

CI run on head 669588f reports success: 172 tests, 0 failures, 0 skipped, including the registered SES-1 control test. I could not rerun it here (pytest not installed), and the JUnit report's timestamp and hostname don't match run.json.
The touched components payments.policy and payments.controls-data are not marked security_sensitive in components.json, so no security review is required.
controls/payments/policy-params.json is a protected path. Control owner Bao Tran (controls-office, outside the author's payments-eng team) approved the head commit.
No acceptance-ledger entry covers policy.py PRIVILEGED_IDLE_MINUTES or the session params, so no earlier evidence lapses.

summary: The change raises Payments' privileged-session idle timeout to 16 minutes, breaching SES-1's approved 15-minute cap. The passing control test only checks the code against the policy value this change also edited, so it shows nothing about the cap. The cited risk acceptance EXC-0255 is valid in approver, expiry and compensating control, but it is scoped to payments.session while the change modifies payments.policy and payments.controls-data, so EXC-1 says it doesn't count. The ticket, approvals, control-owner sign-off and CI are in order, but an uncovered breach of a high-severity product obligation requires rejection.
